signature.name: Calm Wait Safety
signature.description: Does the loader feel calm and steady for everyone, with no strobing, an invisible 5s seam, eased pacing, and a reduced-motion state that still says in progress?

bare-wire.signature_why: Seam is invisible and nothing strobes, but a large dark disc fades in over 0.2s every second like a heartbeat, and the reduced-motion state is a single scar breathing, which is calm but generic.
bare-wire.loved: Honest README and pitch that admit the healing may read as just a pulse; six shapes, fills only, no flashing.
bare-wire.docked: Five identical 1Hz pulses with no directional sense of progress, and the subtle crema-heal idea may be lost at 120px.

warm-hands.signature_why: One slow linear sweep with eased sway and out-of-phase opacity breaths, frame 5.0 verified equal to frame 0.0, no abrupt changes, and a reduced-motion held pour that still breathes so it reads as working on it.
warm-hands.loved: Steady unhurried rotation plus a deliberately composed reduced-motion pose; the loop is seamless in position and velocity.
warm-hands.docked: A turning spiral can still read as a generic spinner at 120px, the stain is fine detail, and SVG child transforms are not compositor-promoted (named honestly).

the-glitch.signature_why: Deliberate sideways band slip plus per-second hard cuts (drop vanishing, ring and pip popping on) add several abrupt changes each second, and the glitch repeats six times in a 30s wait, which is the opposite of calm.
the-glitch.loved: Reduced-motion branch is well thought out (slow pip cross-fades keep a progress cue), and the pitch is candid about the tic risk.
the-glitch.docked: Designing in an intentional hiccup invites anxiety and looks broken to a tired user; hard-cut pips and drop make the pacing busy rather than soothing.
